wslConfig.Raw:
# Dad's MMO Lab -- WSL2 resource limits. Safe to edit by hand; the installer
# will not overwrite this file once it exists. If a WoW server build runs out
# of memory, lower 'processors' and/or raise 'swap' (see the HOWTO).
[wsl2]
memory=16GB
processors=6
swap=10GB
localhostForwarding=true
vmIdleTimeout=60000

# THE ARITHMETIC, corrected 2026-08-01 after this machine crashed mid-build.
#
# AzerothCore's Dockerfile builds with `-j $(($(nproc) + 1))` -- read from the
# pinned checkout, hardcoded inside the RUN with no ARG, so nothing outside the
# image can change it. The Docker VM inherits the limits in this file, so:
#
#     processors = N   ->   N + 1 concurrent C++ compilers   ->   ~2 GB each
#
# The previous setting was processors=8 / memory=16GB, written on 2026-07-31
# with a comment claiming it "keeps ~2.0 GB per parallel compiler against the
# 16GB above". That was wrong by exactly one compiler: 8 processors starts
# NINE, needing ~18 GB against 16. The build over-committed and the machine
# went down.
#
# Now: 6 processors -> 7 compilers -> ~14 GB, inside 20 GB with real headroom
# for the linker peak (larger than a compile job) and the MySQL container
# running beside it. The host has 31.2 GB, so this still leaves ~11 GB for
# Windows.
#
# THE RULE when changing either number: memory >= (processors + 1) * 2 GB,
# plus a few GB of headroom. Raise `memory` before `processors`, never after.
#
# NB `swap` is not a safety net for this. Swapping a C++ link step thrashes the
# disk badly enough to take the desktop down with it, which is what happened.

[experimental]
# autoMemoryReclaim lives HERE, not under [wsl2]. In [wsl2] WSL rejected it
# with "Unknown key 'wsl2.autoMemoryReclaim'" on every single wsl.exe call --
# so it was inert AND noisy.
autoMemoryReclaim=gradual

Images|3.495GB|6.835MB (0%)
Containers|49.15kB|8.192kB (16%)
Local Volumes|10.53GB|0B (0%)
Build Cache|70.75GB|68.39GB

note: C3 server up, 1948 bots online (plateaued). WORKLOAD NOT COMPARABLE TO DESKTOP (100 bots): this server is configured 1600-2000 via the override AC_AI_PLAYERBOT_MIN/MAX_RANDOM_BOTS. Sampled at T0+575s from the container start, matching the desktop protocol point. Distro held open by a sleep holder - WSL force-terminated it once mid-run with the server live.
caveats: ATTRIBUTION: all WSL distros share ONE utility VM and ONE Linux kernel. The 'vmmemWSL' figure is the WHOLE VM, not this backend's share of it. It is attributable to 'arch' only because the preconditions established that no other distro was running.

A memory cap is set in .wslconfig (memory=16GB). Any loaded reading at or near this cap is the CAP, not the demand: the workload may want more and be unable to take it. Do not read a capped figure as 'this backend needs N GB'.

autoMemoryReclaim=gradual is set. Memory freed inside the VM returns to Windows GRADUALLY and on an undocumented schedule, so any single post-stop sample measures the reclaim schedule as much as the workload. Read the 'stopped' SERIES, never one point from it.
The machine-level figures include EVERYTHING running on the box, not just this backend. They are only meaningful against an 'off' baseline taken on the same quiet machine in the same sitting.

Docker was queried during this sample. On this machine a read-only docker command was observed to WAKE a stopped docker-desktop distro and create a fresh WSL VM; if that happened here, the VM generation changed mid-measurement.
Distros Running at sample time: dml-arch.
notMeasured: Per-distro memory. WSL2 runs every distro in ONE VM with ONE kernel, and /proc/meminfo is not namespaced, so a distro asked about memory reports the whole VM's. Two distros running at once cannot be told apart from Windows OR from inside. The harness handles this by REFUSING to sample when more than one is up, not by splitting the number.
The kernel's own share (page cache, slab, tmpfs) within the VM. It is real memory the backend causes to be used, but it belongs to the shared kernel and cannot be assigned to a distro.
Bots actually online. That needs SOAP or MySQL; -BotsOnline records the OPERATOR's claim and is not a measurement.
Disk actually freed. A .vhdx never shrinks, so the disk figures are high-water marks; 'docker system df' gives the engine's logical view, which is the comparable one.

Docker Desktop's Windows-side memory in the Arch column: it is zero only because Desktop is required to be exited. Any user who keeps Desktop installed and running for other work pays it on both backends.
